column4: Font files and fontconfig rules that every program uses to render text
column5: Read as values by all programs drawing text, so a setting not confined to one program (S2.2-13, S2.2-7); removal changes or loses rendering of these glyphs.

column4: Metapackage: dependency record, at most an AppStream metainfo file; installs no program
column5: Removing this record alone leaves every program, rule and setting in place; the computer does and can do the same, so the removal test fails.

column4: Owns directories only, no regular files
column5: Removal deletes at most empty directories; nothing the computer does or can do depends on them, so the removal test fails.
Documents are content: after removal the computer does and can do the same, only the documents themselves are unavailable.

column4: Device firmware files for hardware absent from this machine (virtio, bochs, piix only)
column5: S2.2-16: device firmware the system can change must be recorded; removal test changes nothing here unless attachable devices count. Text decides neither which prevails nor whether attachable hardware counts.

column4: Device-specific rules and data for hardware absent from this machine
column5: Removal changes nothing now but disables such devices if attached later; the removal test does not say whether devices that could be attached count.
S2.2-4 lists contents of databases as content (need not); its rationale (computer does the same) is false here: removal changes what programs do (S2.2-2). Text does not say which governs.

column4: Firmware executed inside QEMU virtual machines as guest code
column5: S2.2-11: code confined in a virtual machine need not be recorded; S2.2-2: without it QEMU cannot start such machines. Two sentences conflict, none prevails.

column4: UEFI boot binaries; whether this machine boots through UEFI is not established
column5: Effect exists only if the firmware boots via UEFI; the inventory (i440fx, no EFI devices listed) does not establish the boot mode, so what it does here is unknown.

column4: Ships systemd unit files defining services or sockets
column5: Unit files let the service manager start a service; after removal the service cannot be started, so something becomes impossible.
